paper.abstract_en: We consider seesaw models with hierarchical Dirac neutrino masses. We show that, barring well known fine-tuned crossing level solutions and given current low energy neutrino experimental data, these always lead to a very hierarchical heavy neutrino spectrum. If the Dirac neutrino masses are assumed not to significantly differ from the up-quark masses, then the intermediate seesaw neutrino ($N_2$) mass falls in the correct range for its decays to explain the matter-antimatter asymmetry of the universe via ($N_2$-)leptogenesis, while the lightest seesaw neutrino decays give a negligible contribution. We show that these conclusions are valid independently of any additional condition on the Dirac neutrino mass matrix. In this way we extend the usual $SO(10)$-inspired leptogenesis scenario, assuming the mismatch between neutrino and charged lepton Dirac mass matrices at the level of the CKM matrix. We find that solutions for inverted ordered neutrino masses become viable. We still find a lower bound on the lightest neutrino mass, $m_1 \gtrsim 10^{-5}\,{\rm eV}$, but this is relaxed by two orders of magnitude. We also consider the special subset of solutions realising strong thermal leptogenesis within this extended scenario, finding that inverted ordering remains incompatible. Our results show how the emergence of the $N_2$-leptogenesis scenario within seesaw models is much more general than thought so far.
